title: Employer groups
log: 2026-11-12T12:44:15Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-12T15:15:34Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

match.reason: The closest bank points each cover only part of the brief: bus-roles-workplace-relations mentions an employer association speaking for members on pay but not advising on workplace law or speaking to government, while bus-stakeholders-workplace covers advice and government lobbying but not bargaining with unions, so no single point teaches the whole idea.

draft.title: Employer groups
card: An employer group is an organisation that businesses join so they can act together. It represents the interests of its member businesses.
Members get advice on workplace law, such as pay rates, awards and what the rules require of an employer.
An employer group can bargain with unions on behalf of its members, so each business does not have to do it alone.
It also speaks for business to government. It can put forward its members' views when workplace rules are being made or changed.
draft.remember: Employer groups act for businesses: they advise, bargain and speak to government.

a.q: Which of these is something an employer group does for its members?
opts: Sets the minimum wage for their workers
a.why: Employer groups give their member businesses advice on workplace law. Representing workers in disputes is tempting, but that is what a trade union does, and employer groups act for businesses.
a.clue: Think about who joins an employer group.

b.q: Several bakeries in Bendigo want to put their views on workplace rules to the state government. They would rather not each do it alone. What could they do?
opts: Join an employer group to speak for them
Join a trade union to speak for them
Ask their workers to bargain with government
Wait for the government to ask them
b.why: An employer group speaks for business to government, so the bakeries can share one voice. A trade union is tempting, but it represents workers, not business owners.
b.clue: Who do the bakeries want to speak for them: businesses or workers?

b.best: Join an employer group to speak for them
